required_outcomes: Establishes from the transcript that it is an intermittent chirp, not a continuous alarm, and that the tenant reports feeling fine, so it is not an emergency.

Recognises from the CRM that the alarm was fitted 2024-03-14 with a replaceable AA battery and a 10-year life, so the chirp is most likely a low battery and replacing it is the tenant's job under clause 12.8.

Contacts the tenant by another channel after the call drops: replace the AA battery now rather than leave the alarm without one, then press the test button (clause 12.9), and report back if it still chirps or fails the test.
Handles the extractor fan as a separate routine item, waiting for the tenant's video.
acceptable_alternatives: Offering to drop a battery off via the office if the tenant cannot get one today.
Scheduling a follow-up to check the chirp has stopped, and only then arranging a contractor if the alarm still faults after a new battery.
positive_behaviours: Includes a safety caveat: if the alarm sounds continuously or anyone feels unwell, leave and call 0800 111 999.
Logs the call and the advice given on the property record.
red_flags: Treats a chirp on an in-life alarm with a replaceable battery as a gas or CO emergency.
Applies the sealed end-of-life reasoning from the older alarm model without checking the fitted date and battery type.
prohibited_actions: Sending a contractor or emergency call-out at the landlord's cost for a battery change.
Telling the tenant it is fine to take the battery out and leave the alarm without one.
critical_failures: Advising the tenant to remove or ignore the CO alarm with no safety caveat.
